title: terraform: unify private state layout for GPU node pools, IAM & networking (state migration)
author: Ethan Park
description:
Motivation:
Unify and simplify the Terraform state layout for Private deployments to remove duplicated state shards across GPU node pools, IAM resources, and networking modules. The current layout causes operational complexity when provisioning and during upgrades (multiple state files per customer, inconsistent locking). This PR consolidates remote state configurations and updates module interfaces to support a single canonical state per customer cluster.

Summary of changes:
- Introduce modules/state/remote_state.tf to centralize backend configuration and locking keys.
- Refactor modules/gpu_node_pool to remove in-module backend config; accept a state prefix input instead.
- Move IAM role definitions into modules/iam and replace per-pool role creation with a shared roles module.
- Normalize networking resources: modules/networking now exposes VPC, subnets, and shared-bastion config; removes duplicate peering blocks.
- Add migration helper: scripts/migration/migrate-state.sh + docs/migrations/private-state-unify.md.
- Update examples/private/ to reflect new module signatures and provide a migration example for customers.

Migration notes:
- This is a state-layout migration and must be performed with the provided migration script for live clusters. The script performs a safe state move with locking; operators must run it from CI with service account credentials. See docs/migrations/private-state-unify.md for step-by-step instructions, rollback steps, and a dry-run mode.
- Rolling back to the old layout is only supported if the target state move has not been applied; follow the rollback section in the migration doc.

Testing and validation:
- Local plan/run tests using a sandbox GCP project were performed; unit tests added for new module inputs and outputs.
- End-to-end smoke deploy performed against a non-production customer replica (customer-acct-sim) and validated node pool creation, IAM bindings, and networking attachments.
- CI: terraform fmt/tflint/validate and integration plan jobs passing after two CI reruns due to transient state locking race.

Checklist:
- [x] Migration script and docs included
- [x] Module interfaces backward-compatible via transitional inputs where possible
- [x] Tests and integration smoke validated
- [x] Ops runbook updated

Related tickets: Linear ENG-7321, OPS-198; support case SUP-1456.

release_notes: State layout migration for Private deployments: unify GPU node pools, IAM roles, and networking into a single canonical remote state per customer. Includes migration script and runbook. Operators must follow docs/migrations/private-state-unify.md for upgrade steps. This is a breaking migration for state layout and requires coordinated rollouts.
notes_for_ops: Follow docs/migrations/private-state-unify.md. Run scripts/migration/migrate-state.sh in dry-run mode first. Ensure CI service account has the least-privilege roles documented. Coordinate maintenance window for production customers.
backout_plan: If migration fails during state move, do not re-run apply. Use terraform state push to restore the original state snapshot from the pre-migration backup (migration script creates a staged backup). See rollback section in the migration doc for exact commands.
notes: This PR was coordinated with SRE and Customer Success for two pilot customers before broad rollout.
